purchases.title: Julian Assange Is Back: What 20 Years of Censorship Resistance Taught Us
purchases.summary:
On September 17, 2026, Julian Assange broke a two-year silence with two words: "I'm back."
From launching WikiLeaks in 2006 and releasing the 2010 War Logs to enduring seven years inside the Ecuadorian Embassy and five years in Belmarsh Prison, Assange's story is the ultimate blueprint of censorship resistance.

This comprehensive analysis explores his journey, the legal battles under the Espionage Act, his 2024 plea deal, and why his legacy directly connects to the cypherpunk movement, Bitcoin, and Nostr.
topics: investigative journalism, free speech, cypherpunk culture, bitcoin & decentralized protocols

purchases.title: Money, Desire, and Honest Weights — 21 Essays
purchases.summary: Twenty-two minutes. Twenty-one essays. From Abraham’s silver weights at Machpelah to Nixon’s 1971 gold window closure to Bitcoin’s fixed supply — the moral case for sound money is older than any central bank. Girard, Banfield, Leviticus, and the Federal Reserve in the same conversation.

purchases.title: Faith as a Way of Knowing
purchases.summary: Not devotional writing — epistemology with a pulse. Plantinga's 'warrant' and 'proper function' run beneath all of it. The Abraham diptych (Genesis 22 and 23) is the center of gravity. Kierkegaard's Johannes de Silentio gives listener a vocabulary for the kind of trust that cannot be explained from the outside. Faith is not opposed to reason — it is a specific form of knowing that reason alone cannot replicate.

purchases.title: AI & the Architecture of Attention
purchases.summary: Nine essays circling a single anxiety: what happens to human knowing when the tools for knowing become autonomous? From prediction markets and moral hazard, through the oracle problem, to AI as coroner rather than killer. The final essay — uploading Kierkegaard to an AI and discovering the machine asked something he hadn't thought to ask himself. The conclusion: AI is not the threat. Formation is the issue.

purchases.title: How Good People Drift into Disaster
purchases.summary: The smallest cluster and the sharpest. Six essays using popular culture the way a theologian uses a parable. Girard's mimetic desire runs beneath every system. You just stop noticing what you're becoming.

Nothing here is exotic, advanced, or meant only for experts. The tools and approaches discussed are not overkill; they are a deliberate mix designed to preserve productivity while significantly improving how much of your life leaks into the open. A key idea running through the article is that privacy and security are not the same thing.
